chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Isa ibn al-Dahhak, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Wonder is shown to the boastful, the proud, and indeed he was created from a drop of fluid, then he will return to be a carcass, and he is, in what is between that, not knowing what will be done with him.'

key_terms.الْفَخُورِ: The proud, one who displays arrogance
key_terms.لِلْمُخْتَالِ: The boastful, one who walks with pride

ai.seo_question: What does the Imam say about the nature of the arrogant person's origin and fate?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) critiques the arrogance of the boastful by highlighting the humble origin of creation from a mere drop of fluid and the inevitable return to being a carcass. This narration underscores the transient nature of worldly status, reminding believers that between birth and death, one remains unaware of their ultimate destiny, a theme central to Shia reflections on humility (tawadu').

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Isa Bin Al Zahhak who said,

‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> wonder at the boastful, the proud, and rather he was Created from a seed, then he would return to be a carcass, and he is, during what is between that, not knowing what would be done with him’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from ‘Isa ibn al-Dahhak who has said the following: “

Abu Ja’far (a.s.) has said, ‘It is astonishing how one acts boastfully and arrogantly, when it is a fact that he is created from sperm and he will soon turn into a carcass and, in between, he does not know what may happen to him.’”
